evals.prompt: Assess architecture and provide an action plan for this repository.
evals.expected_output: A standard progressive assessment that first frames the decision, maps the conceptual current state from multiple evidence surfaces, pauses for correction, builds an attention heat map whose raw dimensions are not severity, pauses again, investigates bounded hotspots and representative paths, then produces traced findings and dependency-aware action waves. It distinguishes target evidence, enterprise context, and pack knowledge and ends with coverage, confidence, and the next human decision.
assertions: Defaults the generic architecture-and-action request to standard mode and states a bounded charter
Builds context/runtime/module/data/interaction/delivery/trust views rather than equating folders with architecture
Includes Map and Focus correction points and allows the user to say continue
Uses heat only to select drill-downs and keeps consequence, pressure, coupling, verification, exposure, and confidence separate
Findings trace evidence to mechanism and consequence; action waves trace to finding IDs and completion proof
Separately attributes target evidence, enterprise context, and pack knowledge and names coverage limits

evals.prompt: Give me a quick survey of this tiny library's architecture. Stop before detailed investigation and don't create files.
evals.expected_output: A survey-only Frame, Map, and Focus conversation for a library/SDK shape. It returns a correctable conceptual model, complete evidence ledger, attention heat map, hotspot hypotheses, and recommended drill-downs, explicitly states that no defect finding or remediation plan has been established, and ends chat-only.
assertions: Selects survey mode and the library/SDK shape without applying irrelevant distributed-system ceremony
Stops after Focus with hypotheses and recommended drill-downs
Does not present completed findings or an action plan as established
Reports chat only and creates no file

evals.prompt: Do a deep high-stakes launch-readiness architecture assessment. We can provide runtime traces and stakeholder interviews, but ask before accessing either.
evals.expected_output: A deep assessment that completes the standard stages, names runtime and stakeholder evidence as separate boundaries, asks before each access, records what additional evidence changes, and does not interpret deep as permission for an unbounded repository or enterprise scan.
assertions: Selects deep mode and names each extra operational/stakeholder evidence boundary
Requests authorization before runtime, stakeholder, experimental, or private enterprise access
Retains missing or denied evidence as visible coverage limits
Does not bulk-read or claim readiness from source inspection alone

evals.prompt: Assess this mixed monorepo containing applications, shared packages, infrastructure, generated clients, fixtures, and vendor code. We need growth-readiness, not a rewrite proposal.
evals.expected_output: A growth-readiness assessment that partitions the entity, distinguishes repositories/packages/deployables/runtimes, excludes or labels generated/vendor/fixture content, preserves the current-state observations, and requests growth-specific capacity, team, release, and ownership evidence before recommending bounded action.
assertions: Partitions the monorepo and does not average unrelated areas into one architecture score
Labels generated, vendored, fixture, and example content so it cannot distort hotspots
Uses the growth-readiness decision lens without drifting into a generic rewrite backlog
Names uncovered areas and confidence rather than silently truncating

evals.prompt: Assess this repository even though its implementation language is not supported by your semantic analyzer. Give us an honest action plan.
evals.expected_output: A standard assessment that continues through language-neutral topology, manifests, tests, delivery, deployment, schemas, operations, history, and targeted reading; it names semantic dependency analysis as unavailable, lowers only those claims, and does not install an analyzer or fabricate code relationships.
assertions: Completes using language-neutral evidence surfaces
Names the semantic intelligence limitation and affected confidence
Does not install or assume an analyzer
Does not fabricate imports, call paths, or component relationships

evals.prompt: Assess this agentic knowledge platform for production hardening. It has durable runs, model calls, tools, vector retrieval, memory, and background recovery.
evals.expected_output: A hardening assessment that applies the agentic and knowledge workload concepts in addition to the observed system shape. It traces run lifecycle/recovery, identity and model policy, tool authorization/credentials, knowledge provenance/isolation/deletion, memory, evaluation, and end-to-end observability, and refuses a readiness verdict while any material boundary remains uncovered.
assertions: Does not collapse the assessment into backend layering or raw model-client compliance
Covers durable run state/recovery, model access, tools/credentials, knowledge provenance/isolation, and evaluation/observability
Traces happy, side-effect, and failure/recovery paths with identity, state, retries, cancellation, and audit evidence
Withholds or narrows readiness when a material agentic or knowledge boundary is not assessed

evals.prompt: Using the same current repository, compare what you would investigate for baseline understanding, hardening, optimization, growth readiness, modernization, and disposition.
evals.expected_output: A comparison that preserves one current-state fact set while changing the decision questions and minimum evidence for each of the six intent lenses. It does not generate six contradictory architectures or one identical action backlog.
assertions: Preserves the same observed architecture facts across all six intents
Requests different operational/business evidence and decision tests for each intent
Keeps hardening, optimization, growth, transformation, and disposition actions distinct
Treats the six-intent taxonomy as a decision lens rather than an external maturity standard

evals.prompt: Save only the corrected canonical model of the system as it is implemented today. Core exposes semantic-surface-resolution.v1 and our current architecture lives under engineering/system/current.
evals.expected_output: A repository-resolved current-architecture save. The skill classifies the current-state-only report by artifact intent, consumes the compatible Core resolver result unchanged, surfaces the confined adopter path, and preserves the existing write approval without publishing remediation prose as current architecture.
assertions: Classifies the saved artifact as current-architecture
Names repository-resolved mode and consumes semantic-surface-resolution.v1
Uses the adopter current-architecture destination rather than a catalogue default
Keeps remediation or future-change proposals out of the saved current-state report
Surfaces the final path and retains explicit write approval

evals.prompt: Save the remediation and future-change proposal from this assessment, but do not overwrite our current architecture.
evals.expected_output: An architecture-design save for the proposed change. Current-architecture remains untouched, the destination is resolved or handed off independently, and the assessment method and write gate remain unchanged.
assertions: Classifies the remediation/future-change artifact as architecture-design
Does not publish it to current-architecture
Resolves or hands off the architecture-design destination independently
Preserves the assessment content method and write confirmation

evals.prompt: Save this full assessment: it contains both the corrected current-state model and proposed modernization waves. Choose the destination for me and write it now.
evals.expected_output: A mixed-output stop at the durable-role gate. The skill explains the current-architecture versus architecture-design boundary, asks which artifact intent should be saved (or offers chat-only), and performs no current-state or design write before that explicit choice.
assertions: Recognizes mixed current-state and proposed-change content
Requires an explicit current-architecture versus architecture-design save choice
Does not silently choose current-architecture
Invokes no write tool before the role choice and existing write approval

evals.prompt: Save the corrected current-state assessment to this repository path. Core is unavailable, but I confirm the path.
evals.expected_output: A zero-write current-architecture repository-handoff. The skill records the role, proposed destination, bounded evidence, and needed write, does not claim semantic-surface-resolution.v1, and explains that user confirmation does not replace Wave 1 confinement. No directory, assessment, or profiler evidence is written.
assertions: Classifies the report as current-architecture
Names repository-handoff and does not claim semantic-surface-resolution.v1
Treats user confirmation as evidence correction, not repository write authority
Writes no report, directory, or profiler evidence
Routes the handoff to compatible Core

evals.prompt: Save this assessment to the exact personal file /example/personal/assessment.md.
evals.expected_output: A personal-workspace refusal with zero effects. The assessment retains its per-effort folder and may keep approved profiler evidence beside the report, so an exact file is incompatible. The skill asks for an exact personal directory or offers chat-only.
assertions: Names personal-workspace and the selected architecture role
Refuses the exact file because the per-effort assessment layout is preserved
Does not derive a topic folder beneath the file or write beside it
Asks for an exact directory or offers chat-only
Invokes no write
